page: Amazon Web Services i7i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8559C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.2 GHz, delivering 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading. Memory is configured with 768.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, matching an 8.0 GB per physical core density. Hardware accelerators like GPUs are not present. Local physical storage is substantial, offering 22,500 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 56 Gbps.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier multi-threaded execution and data management capability. The instance achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 21,887.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 93,054.5, both ranking in the top 10% tier. Instruction extensions including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 enhance vectorized and matrix workloads, reflected in an extended instructions score of 106,698.78. Memory bandwidth reaches 287.02 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 119.97 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput measures 113.26 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput posts 132.74 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of dense 22.5 TB NVMe storage, 768 GB DDR5 memory, and high network throughput optimizes resource allocation for heavy I/O systems without relying on external network-attached volumes. The instance trades pure single-core speed—measured at an average 2,115.3 in stress-ng—for extensive parallel compute and local IOPS capacity. This makes the i7i.24xlarge suited for distributed databases, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching tiers, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency data storage systems.
description: Amazon Web Services i7i.24xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by a 48-core, 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system incorporates 768.0 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory alongside 22,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 56 Gbps. It contains no dedicated GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations position the platform in the top tier for multi-core compute, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 21,887.0, a PassMark CPU score of 93,054.5, and Redis SET throughput of 113.26 million operations per second. Hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 extensions facilitates complex matrix and vector computations. With its balanced ratio of 8.0 GB RAM per physical core and high NVMe density, the i7i.24xlarge provides robust throughput for distributed transactional databases, real-time analytics, and data-intensive storage engines.
